fit: printed case proportion at presentation versus later subacute course
assessment: The 1984 retrospective series identifies 121 confirmed and 31 probable Creutzfeldt–Jakob cases, with possible diagnoses handled separately. In printed tables 4 and 5, visual hallucinations are recorded at presentation in 1% and during the subacute course in 17%. These are proportions of patients with the sign in a different disease and time window. The series supplies no dried fig exposure or Parkinson episode-rate estimate.

fit: visual hallucination status matched for cognition and age
assessment: A structural MRI study compares 25 people with Parkinson disease and current chronic visual hallucinations with 25 without hallucinations, matched for age and cognitive status. The authors assess visuoperceptive regions and separate cognition from hallucination group status. This comparison does not quantify a change in visual episode frequency after a documented food intake.

fit: authentic 1872 first edition distinguishes fresh from dried practice
assessment: Printed page 439 assigns reported excitement to heavy fresh fig intake during harvest. The dried-fruit discussion concerns customary use and preservation. The 2003 printing repeats this account, so it contributes no second independent observation. No diagnosed Parkinson or visual symptom outcome is documented.

fit: frozen ground fig fruit added to chow and inflammatory measurements in Alzheimer-model mice
assessment: The study prepared fresh fruit by freezing and grinding it, and used separate fig, date and pomegranate diets. The authors measure inflammatory and other biomarkers. This is neither a clinical Parkinson comparison nor a visual episode measure. Related animal reports may share animal or formulation lineage.

fit: abstract of fig-supplemented chow and behavior in a transgenic Alzheimer model
assessment: The published abstract reports behavioral task results for fig-supplemented mice, with full preparation and animal lineage unresolved. Maze, movement and anxiety-like scores do not convey visual hallucination frequency. The related biomarker report cannot establish this study's preparation.

fit: immediate clinical fig reaction with separate fresh and dried skin tests
assessment: The original poster summarizes an immediate reaction to fig ingestion with unspecified prepared form. Separate skin tests show sensitization to fresh and dried material. The controlled intake challenge did not occur; neither visual episodes nor clinical Parkinson effects were measured.

fit: fresh and sun-dried culinary preparations in simulated digestion
assessment: The original summary reports differences by fig variety and compound in a dialysed in vitro digestion fraction. Several measures increase after drying, while the examined anthocyanins are undetected in the dried fraction. The exposure is a food matrix assay and clinical effects remain unmeasured.

fit: dried figs as a tested product in a calcium digestion study
assessment: The primary abstract places dried figs among products with calcium bioaccessibility below 10% under static in vitro digestion. Exact product data await the full report. The measured fraction has no direct Parkinson visual outcome.
